readerQuestion: How can Home Assistant remind me which bins to put out tomorrow, including recycling weeks and changed holiday pickup dates?
directAnswer: Use one dedicated collection calendar, supplied by a provider feed when appropriate or maintained with built-in Local calendar. At 7 pm, query the whole next local date and send one message joining the collection names. Correct exceptions in the calendar using the collector's notice. First enter confirmed pickup dates and test a plain phone notification. The example needs Home Assistant running at the scheduled time, does not replay missed attempts, and cannot prove the bins are outside.
originalContribution: The #automation section provides a complete single-calendar YAML walkthrough that queries tomorrow's midnight-to-midnight interval, joins simultaneous collections, removes duplicate titles and stops an empty list. The #worked-example table applies it to September 10 and 17 hypothetical Thursday pickups, a two-bin day, a move to Friday September 18 and an empty day. The #verification procedure separates manual action testing from the clock-trigger test; #troubleshooting maps six symptoms to the relevant correction. Local YAML/Jinja fixtures verified empty, single, two-bin and duplicate-title output, a visible missing-calendar error, month/year rollover and 23/25-hour local-day intervals. These are configuration calculations, not a deployed Home Assistant test.
limitations: Documentation research and local parsing/template fixtures only. No physical hardware, phone delivery, municipal provider, running Home Assistant automation, bin movement or completed collection was tested. Example dates are explicitly fictional. Local entries need ongoing maintenance; remote dates can be stale and Remote Calendar documents a 24-hour default upstream fetch interval. The sample covers one calendar and has no acknowledgement, retry or startup catch-up. The AI-generated cover is an illustrative household scene. Browser availability and passing checks establish neither Google indexing nor traffic recovery.
proofreadFixes: The first proofreading pass found that empty-day testing was impractical when real pickups were present. Added a separate temporary Bin reminder test calendar, instructions to replace both IDs temporarily, and explicit restoration afterwards so real collection entries need not be removed. Replaced the unclear phrase 'subtracts the evening' with 'checks one day ahead.' Replaced 'mismatched response key' with a concrete calendar-ID mismatch explanation. Narrowed the research-method wording to YAML syntax and sample date/message calculations so it does not imply a Home Assistant execution test. Rechecked the four-bullet TLDR, first-section answer, named calendar choices, holiday caveat, visible By Tara Home link, fictional-date disclosure and professional source labels. Final automated plain-English proofreading verdict: PASS; no human or expert review is claimed.

claimChecks.claim: Local calendar can be added through Settings, Devices & services, Add integration and stores events used for automations.
calendar.get_events accepts start_date_time and an exclusive end_date_time and returns an events list keyed by calendar, with event summary fields.
The 2026.9.1 calendar action converts its supplied start and end times to local time before obtaining calendar events; the example constructs midnight values from local dates.
A false condition inside an automation action sequence stops later actions, allowing an empty collection list to produce no phone message.
Remote Calendar reads a supplied calendar URL and documents a default 24-hour update interval after its startup fetch.
Calendar entity attributes represent only the next event and are insufficient for enumerating simultaneous collection events.
Companion App notifications can use the phone-specific notify.mobile_app action with a title and message.
Local Push is a separate WebSocket delivery path with local connection requirements, distinct from ordinary Apple or Google push services.
